BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r3.claim: Migration for the sake of religion is among the righteous deeds of those who believe and act well.

BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r4.claim: Lanubawwi'annahum means We will settle them; al-Taj defines the root as placing someone in a place.
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r4.anchor: قال في "التاج" : النبوء (كسى را جابي فرآوردن)

BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r5.claim: The chambers are lofty palaces of pearl, emerald, and ruby; Heaven is above while Hell is below, and viewing water and greenery from a chamber is especially delightful.
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r5.anchor: قصورا عالية من الدر والزبرجد والياقوت وإنما قال ذلك لأن الجنة في جهة عالية

BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r6.claim: The phrase streams beneath them describes the chambers, and the believers remain there forever.
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r6.anchor: صفة لغرفا {خالدين فيها} أي : ماكثين في تلك الغرف

BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p352#3/r7.claim: The excellent reward is for people who perform righteous deeds.

FARRA:v2p318/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p318/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p318/r2.claim: The common reading لنبوئنهم means We will settle them in dwellings; Ibn Masʿūd and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read لنثوينهم, “settle them” in the sense of staying.
FARRA:v2p318/r2.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق أن ابن مسعود قرأها (لنثوينهم)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r1.claim: لنبوئنهم means We will settle them in dwellings.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r2.claim: The alternative لنثوينهم derives from ثويت بالمكان, meaning I stayed there.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p338#7/r2.anchor: فهو من "ثويت بالمكان" أي أقمت به

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak explains that God will lodge the believers in rooms from Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك لنبوئنهم من الجنة يقول : من الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r2.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r2.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym distinguishes the parallel wording in 16:41: its lodging is a reward in this world, while 29:58 promises rooms in Paradise as the afterlife reward.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r2.anchor: كان الربيع بن خيثم يقول : هذا الحرف في النحل . الذين هاجروا في الله من بعد ما ظلموا لنبوئنهم في الدنيا حسنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r3.claim: The Prophet says Paradise contains rooms whose outside can be seen from inside and whose inside can be seen from outside; they are prepared for those who feed others, greet people, maintain prayer and fasting, and pray at night while others sleep.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r3.anchor: ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حدثه ان في الجنة غرفا يرى ظاهرها من باطنها وباطنها من ظاهرها

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the rivers run beneath the trees in the gardens.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير تجري من تحتها الانهار يعني تحتها الانهار تحت الشجر في البساتين

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r5.claim: Muqatil explains that the good reward of those who work is Paradise, the reward for obeying God.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل قوله : نعم اجر العاملين يقول : اجر العاملين بطاعة الله الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r6.speaker: محمد بن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains the workers' good reward as the recompense of the obedient.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3077/r6.anchor: قال : محمد بن اسحاق نعم اجر العاملين قال : هي ثواب المطيعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r10.claim: The promise of Gardens encourages believers who act righteously; lanubawwiʾannahum means to settle them securely, and ghurafan is the second object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r10.anchor: ثم وعد المؤمنين العاملين بسكنى الجنة تحريضا منه تعالى، وذكر الجزاء الذي ينالونه، وقرأ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r11.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r11.claim: They read lanuthwiyannahum from athwā, meaning to make them dwell; this reading is also attributed to Ali, Ibn Masʿud, al-Rabiʿ b. Khuthaym, Ibn Waththab, and Talha.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «لنثوينهم» من أثوى يثوي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r12.claim: Another reading doubles the thāʾ rather than using hamza, so ghurafan is accusative after dropping the preposition fī; Yaʿqub reads with yāʾ and Ibn ʿAmir has ḍamma vowels on ghuraf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p323#3/r12.anchor: وقرأها بعضهم «لنثوينهم» بفتح الثاء وتشديد الواو معدى بالتضعيف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r1.claim: These readers use “لنبوئنهم,” meaning that God will settle the believers in the chambers of Paradise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر لنبوئنهم بالباء أي لننزلنهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r2.claim: These readers use “لنثوينهم,” from dwelling somewhere; al-Zajjāj explains that the verb means to reside and its causative means to lodge someone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p282/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف لنثوينهم بالثاء وهو من ثويت بالمكان إذا أقمت به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r4.claim: God will settle faithful workers forever in high chambers beneath which flow rivers of water, wine, honey, and milk, to direct as they wish; these chambers are an excellent reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p290/r4.anchor: لنسكننهم منازل عالية في الجنة تجري من تحتها الأنهار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.claim: The Prophet says God prepared transparent chambers for those who feed others, speak well, fast, and pray while people sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p292/r2.anchor: أعدها الله لمن أطعم الطعام، وأطاب الكلام، وأباح الصيام، وأقام الصلاة

JISHUMI:v8p5586/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5586/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v8p5586/r6.claim: They read “lanuthwiyannahum” with thāʾ, meaning to lodge them; the others read “lanubawwiʾannahum” with bāʾ, meaning to settle them in a dwelling.
JISHUMI:v8p5586/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: لنثوينهم بالثاء من أثويته منزلا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r13.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r13.claim: They read the verb as لنثوينهم, from dwelling for a long stay.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r13.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { لنثوينهم } بالثاء من الثواء وهو طول المقام

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r14.claim: The other readers have لنبوئنهم, meaning God will settle the believers in lofty chambers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r14.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالباء { لنبوئنهم } معناه لنسكننهم أعالي البيوت

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r15.claim: Chambers combine elevation above ordinary houses with cleaner air and a more pleasant, dry dwelling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r15.anchor: الغرف لا تستقر إلا فوق البيوت فصار فيها جمع بين أمرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r16.speaker: أبو مالك الأشعري
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r16.claim: The Prophet described transparent chambers prepared for those who feed others, speak kindly, keep prayer and fasting, and pray at night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p290/r16.anchor: روى أبو مالك الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( إن في الجنة غرفا

MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.claim: God reminds migrants that everyone dies and returns for judgment; faithful, righteous migrants receive eternal rooms with rivers, and those patient through migration trust God despite lacking money or livelihood in Medina.
MUQATIL:29:56-63/r2.anchor: ثم خوفهم الموت ليهاجروا، فقال تعالى: { كل نفس ذآئقة الموت ثم إلينا ترجعون } [آية: 57]

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r1.claim: God will settle believers in lofty chambers of Paradise; the wording means lodging them there to stay.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا ﴾ لننزلهم من الجنة علالى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r2.speaker: كوفي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r2.claim: The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read a form from thawā, meaning to stay, rather than the majority reading from lodging them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r2.anchor: لبثوينهم كوفى غير عاصم من الثواء وهو النزول للاقامة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r3.claim: The verb is made to take both believers and chambers either by analogy with lodging them, deleting a preposition, or construing the locative as an object.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r3.anchor: والوجه في تعديته إلى ضمير المؤمنين وإلى الغرف أما أجراؤه مجرى لننزلنهم لنؤوينهم أو حذف الجار

NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p263#5/r4.claim: The text notes a pause at العاملين depending on the following syntactic analysis, but the excerpt breaks off before completing it.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r9.claim: God promises believing doers of good Paradise as encouragement, then describes them as those who patiently endure and rely on their Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:56-59/r9.anchor: ثم وعد المؤمنين العاملين بسكنى الجنة تحريضا منه تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.claim: These readers use lanuthwiyannahum, with thāʾ from dwelling, meaning that God will grant rooms in which they reside.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r4.anchor: { لنثوينهم } بالثاء مكان الباء من الثوى

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r5.speaker: رويس عن يعقوب والجحدري والسلمي
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r5.claim: These readers use liyubawwiʾannahum with yāʾ instead of nūn; the other readers use lanubawwiʾannahum, meaning God will settle them in rooms.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r6.anchor: أي «لننزلهم» { غرفا } جمع غرفة وهي العلية المشرفة

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r7.speaker: سهل بن سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r7.claim: Muslim reports from Sahl ibn Saʿd that inhabitants of Paradise's chambers are seen from below like a bright star on the horizon because of their different ranks; they are believers who affirm the messengers, not Prophets alone.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r8.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from ʿAlī that the rooms are transparent inside and out and belong to those who speak well, feed others, fast regularly, and pray at night while people sleep.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:57-60/r8.anchor: هي لمن أطاب الكلام وأطعم الطعام وأدام الصيام وصلى لله بالليل

SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r1.claim: والذين آمنوا permits the common opening and الاشتغال analyses.
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r1.anchor: والذين آمنوا }: يجوز فيه الوجهان المشهوران: الابتداء والاشتغال

SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r2.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r2.claim: The two Kufan readers read لنثوينهم from lodging or dwelling; the rest read لنبوئنهم from settling someone in a place.
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r2.anchor: والأخوان قرآ بثاء مثلثة ساكنة بعد النون، وياء مفتوحة بعد الواو من الثواء

SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r3.claim: On the lodging reading, غرفا can be an object by construing أثوى as causative like أنزل, or a specialized adverb, or accusative after an omitted preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r3.anchor: و " غرفا " على القراءة الأولى: إما مفعول به على تضمين " أثوى " أنزل، فيتعدى لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r4.claim: On the settling reading, غرفا is the second object of بوأ, which also governs a destination with لام in 22:26.
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r4.anchor:
وأما في القراءة الثانية فمفعول ثان، لأن " بوأ " يتعدى لاثنين، قال تعالى:
تبوىء المؤمنين مقاعد

SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r5.claim: A reading لنثوينهم with doubled consonant makes the verb transitive by gemination just as hamza does.
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r5.anchor: وقد قرئ " لنثوينهم " بالتشديد مع الثاء المثلثة، عدي بالتضعيف كما عدي بالهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:58/r6.claim: تجري is an adjective qualifying غرفا.

RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r1.claim: The believers’ promised reward contrasts with the Hell surrounding unbelievers and their punishment for their deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r1.anchor: بين ما يكون للمؤمنين وقت الرجوع إليه كما بين من قبل ما يكون للكافرين بقوله : { وإن جهنم لمحيطة بالكافرين }

RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r2.claim: The mention of chambers above believers signals their elevated rank: unlike unbelievers beneath layers of fire, the believers occupy the highest level, with nothing above them.
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r2.anchor: فيكونون في أعلى عليين ، فلم يذكر فوقهم شيئا إشارة إلى علو مرتبتهم وارتفاع منزلتهم

RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r3.claim: Fire beneath the unbelievers hurts when aligned with and touching their feet; water beneath the believers’ chambers is pleasurable regardless of its distance or position.
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r3.anchor: فقال في النار من تحت أرجلهم ليحصل الألم بها ، وقال ههنا من تحت الغرف لحصول اللذة به كيف كان

RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r4.claim: The command “taste” the punishment would signal the end of a hired worker’s relationship, while “excellent is the wage” comforts believers without suggesting their reward relationship ends.
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r4.anchor: وذلك لأن لفظ الأمر يدل على انقطاع التعلق / بعده

RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r5.claim: Unbelievers’ punishment remains permanently without increase, whereas believers’ reward keeps increasing, as indicated by “the best and more”; unbelievers’ endless duration is established elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v25p75/r5.anchor: الذي يصل إلى الكافر يدوم من غير زيادة والذي يصل إلى المؤمن يزداد على الدوام

STUDYQURAN:29:58/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r1.claim: After returning to God, each soul learns its place in the Hereafter; believers receive lofty Garden abodes, elsewhere described as abodes above abodes.
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r1.anchor: After souls have returned to God, each is informed of its place in the Hereafter. Believers are given lofty abodes of the Garden, which are elsewhere described as lofty abodes above which are lofty abodes (39:20).

STUDYQURAN:29:58/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r2.claim: A report says the Garden’s transparent rooms are prepared for those who feed others, speak well, pray and fast continually, and pray at night while others sleep.
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r2.anchor: Regarding them the Prophet is reported to have said, “In the Garden there are rooms whose outside can be seen from the inside

STUDYQURAN:29:58/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r3.claim: The promise to settle believers alludes to the hardship of emigration and assures those who leave things for God of lofty abodes in the Hereafter, if not in this life.
STUDYQURAN:29:58/r3.anchor: That God shall settle them alludes to the difficulties some may confront in emigrating, addressed in v. 56

TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to urge believers to leave polytheist Mecca for Muslim Medina, persevere in worship, and obey sincerely: every living soul dies and returns to God.
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r1.anchor: الشرك من مكة، إلى أرض الإسلام المدينة، فإن أرضي واسعة، فاصبروا على عبادتي، وأخلصوا طاعتي

TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r2.claim: Those who believe God and His Messenger and obey His commands and avoid prohibitions will be settled in lofty chambers of Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r2.anchor: يعني: صدقوا الله ورسوله، فيما جاء به من عند الله

TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r3.claim: The two readings, lanubawwiʾannahum and lanuthwiyannahum, are both famous and acceptable; both mean that God will lodge them, one from providing a dwelling and the other from settling someone in a residence.
TAB-FULL:v18p435#2/r3.anchor: فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب، وذلك أن قوله: {لنبوئنهم} [النحل: 41]

TAB-FULL:v18p437/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p437/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p437/r1.claim: The patient face harm from polytheists and persevere in obedience and jihad against God's enemies.
TAB-FULL:v18p437/r1.anchor: المشركين في الدنيا، وما كانوا يلقون منهم، وعلى العمل بطاعة الله وما يرضيه، وجهاد أعدائه

TAB-FULL:v18p437/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p437/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p437/r2.claim: They trust God for provision and victory; confidence in God's victory prevents retreat, and what God apportioned as provision will not pass them by.
TAB-FULL:v18p437/r2.anchor: المشركين في الدنيا، وما كانوا يلقون منهم، وعلى العمل بطاعة الله

TABATABAI:29:56-59/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r6.claim: The promise of elevated rooms describes the reward for faith and good works and urges believers to endure and trust God; tabwīʾ means settling someone permanently, and ghuraf are lofty rooms.
TABATABAI:29:56-59/r6.anchor: بيان لأجر الإيمان والعمل الصالح بعد الموت والرجوع إلى الله وفيه حث وترغيب للمؤمنين على الصبر في الله والتوكل على الله

TABRISI:29:58-60/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r1.speaker: يحيى عن أبي بكر وهشام
TABRISI:29:58-60/r1.claim: These readers use the third-person ya in yarjiʿūn; the others read the second-person ta, shifting from the preceding third-person phrasing like iyyāka naʿbudu after al-ḥamdu lillāh.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r1.anchor: قرأ يرجعون بالياء يحيى عن أبي بكر وهشام والباقون بالتاء

TABRISI:29:58-60/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
TABRISI:29:58-60/r2.claim: The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read lanuthwiyannahum with tha; the others read lanubawwiʾannahum with ba.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r2.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم لنثوينهم بالثاء والباقون لنبوئنهم بالباء

TABRISI:29:58-60/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r3.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:29:58-60/r3.claim: The ba reading means settle them and is supported by the Qur'anic wording about Israel and Abraham; its lām may be extra, or the verb may answer Abraham's prayer with its object omitted.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r3.anchor: حجة من قرأ لنبوئنهم بالباء قوله ولقد بوأنا بني إسرائيل مبوء صدق

TABRISI:29:58-60/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:29:58-60/r4.claim: The tha reading means make them dwell, supported by thāwiyan and poetry; because the verb takes a preposition, the absence of one in the verse needs explanation.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r4.anchor: ومن قرأ لنثوينهم فحجته قوله وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين

TABRISI:29:58-60/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:29:58-60/r5.claim: Abu al-Hasan dislikes al-Aʿmash's reading min al-jannati ghurafan because one does not say athwaytuhu al-dāra.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r5.anchor: قرأ الأعمش لنثوينهم من الجنة غرفا ولا يعجبني لأنك لا تقول أثويته الدار

TABRISI:29:58-60/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r6.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:29:58-60/r6.claim: Abu ʿAli explains al-Aʿmash's reading by positing an omitted preposition, as when one says to settle them in rooms, and cites similar deletion.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r6.anchor: ووجهه أنه كان في الأصل لنثوينهم من الجنة في غرف

TABRISI:29:58-60/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:58-60/r7.claim: Khālidīna is an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in the verb.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r7.anchor: نصب على الحال من الهاء والميم

TABRISI:29:58-60/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60/r10.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
TABRISI:29:58-60/r10.claim: The first verse was revealed concerning vulnerable believers in Mecca who were ordered to migrate.
TABRISI:29:58-60/r10.anchor: نزلت الآية الأولى في المستضعفين من المؤمنين بمكة أمروا بالهجرة عنها

TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r5.claim: Those promised rooms are the believers who migrated; God will settle them in elevated chambers beneath which rivers flow.
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r5.anchor: أي لننزلنهم { من الجنة غرفا } أي علالي عاليات

TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes their chambers as palaces of pearl, emerald, and ruby in Paradise.
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r6.anchor: لنسكننهم غرف الدر والزبرجد والياقوت ولننزلنهم قصور الجنة

TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r7.claim: They remain there through God's enduring existence; these chambers are an excellent reward for those who work for Him.
TABRISI:29:58-60#2/r7.anchor: نعم أجر العاملين } لله تلك الغرف

THALABI:v7p288/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p288/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p288/r2.claim: The promised rooms are elevated chambers in Paradise.

THALABI:v7p288/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p288/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p288/r3.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Khalaf read the verb with tāʾ; the other readers use yāʾ.
THALABI:v7p288/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بالتاء، غيرهم بالياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the promised rooms are made of pearls, rubies, and emeralds.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r2.claim: Muqātil glosses the verb as lodging them; this supports the common reading lanubawwiʾannahum, from settling someone in a dwelling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r2.anchor: مقاتل: يعني لننزلنهم (¬3). وهذا يدل على صحة قراءة العامة: {لنبوئنهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r3.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, like ʿAbd Allāh and al-Aʿmash, read lanuthwiyannahum, from thawa, to stay or reside.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (لنثوينهم) وهي قراءة عبد الله والأعمش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r4.claim: Thawā means to stay; thaway means a guest because the guest stays with the host, and the reading relates to the expression for residing among Midian’s people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله: {وما كنت ثاويا في أهل مدين} [القصص: 45] أي: مقيما نازلا فيهم، والثوي: الضيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says thawa is to reside and athwaytuhu is to lodge someone; the transitive form takes a second object.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r5.anchor: الزجاج: يقال: ثوى الرجل إذا أقام، وأثويته إذا أنزلته منزلا يقيم فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r6.speaker: حسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r6.claim: Ḥassān’s line about staying among Quraysh for over ten years supplies poetic evidence for thawa as reside.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r6.anchor: ثوى في قريش بضع عشرة حجة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r7.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash dislikes al-Aʿmash’s reading because Arabic does not say athwaytuhu al-dār.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r7.anchor: الأخفش: قرأ الأعمش: {لنثوينهم من الجنة غرفا} قال: ولا يعجبني ذلك؛ لأنك لا تقول: أثويته الدار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r8.claim: Abū ʿAlī defends the reading by positing an omitted preposition: the original sense is to lodge them in rooms, as in other omitted-preposition constructions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r8.anchor: أبو علي: ووجه هذه القراءة كان في الأصل: لنثوينهم من الجنة في غرف، وحذف الجار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r9.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r9.claim: He supports the omitted preposition by constructions that treat a specified place like an unmarked locative, citing the fox on the road and going to Syria, and a report with or without ilā before the lavatory.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r9.anchor: الغرف وإن كانت مختصة، فقد أجريت المختصة من هذه الظروف مجرى غير المختص

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p549/r10.claim: The common reading is supported by the verse in which the faithful say they will settle wherever they wish in Paradise.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās locates the rivers beneath the chambers and connects their description to the water of Paradise elsewhere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: يريد تحت الغرف الأنهار، كما وصف تبارك وتعالى: {من ماء غير آسن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r2.claim: Remaining forever means they stay there without dying, aging, or falling ill.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r2.anchor: مقيمين فيها لا يموتون، ولا يهرمون، ولا يسقمون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r3.claim: The excellent reward is for the emigrants and Helpers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r3.anchor: نعم أجر العاملين} قال: يريد المهاجرين والأنصار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r4.claim: Muqātil says the reward is for those who work for God; the sentence has an understood complement, namely the chambers or Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p552/r4.anchor: مقاتل: {نعم أجر العاملين} لله (¬1). وفي الآية حذف يتم به الكلام، كأنه قيل: نعم أجر العاملين الغرف أو الجنة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:55-58/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:55-58/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:55-58/r4.claim: God will settle the believers who do good in rooms of Paradise, meaning its palaces.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638/r4.claim: God will settle believers who do good in Garden chambers with rivers beneath; they remain there forever, neither dying nor leaving.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p638#2/r1.claim: “How excellent the reward of the workers” means their excellent reward is Paradise.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r1.claim: Hamza and Kisai read لنثوينهم with thāʾ; the other readers use لنبوئنهم with bāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r1.anchor: اختلفوا في قوله سبحانه: لنبوئنهم [العنكبوت/ 58] في الباء والثاء، فقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (لنثوينهم) بالثاء، وقرأ الباقون: لنبوئنهم بالباء .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r2.claim: Abu Zayd supports بوأنا as establishing someone in a dwelling; the cited verses fit that verb, which can also be read through Abraham's prayer with an object understood.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو زيد: بوأنا فلانا منزلا تبويئا، فما حكى أبو زيد. حجة لمن قرأ لنبوئنهم من الجنة غرفا

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r3.claim: ثوى means to stay or lodge; although أبو الحسن objects that أثويته الدار is not idiomatic, Abu Ali takes the construction as originally meaning lodge them in rooms, with the preposition omitted.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p438#2/r3.anchor: ووجهه أنه كان في الأصل: لنثوينهم من الجنة في غرف، كما تقول: لننزلنهم من الجنة في غرف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p440/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p440/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p440/r1.claim: Arabic can omit a preposition before a place noun even when it names a specific location; this supports supplying في before غرف in the reading لنثوينهم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p440/r1.anchor: فقد أجريت المختصة من هذه الظروف مجرى غير المختصة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r2.claim: لنبوئنهم with bāʾ means settle them in chambers, supported by 2:8; the thāʾ form means lodge them, supported by the description of Moses as ثاويا in Midian.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p281#2/r2.anchor: فالحجة لمن قرأ بالنون والباء أنه أراد لننزلنهم من الجنة غرفا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r5.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p501/r5.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read لنثوينهم with thāʾ; the remaining readers use لنبوئنهم with bāʾ.

QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#1/r1.claim: The th-w-y reading emphasizes taking up long residence in the chambers rather than the act of settlement associated with b-w-ʾ.
QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#1/r1.anchor: From th-w-y (to reside/dwell): canonical variant shifts root from b-w-ʾ

QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#2/r1.claim: This hamza-removal form keeps the b-w-ʾ root and is semantically identical to the standard reading.
QIRAAT-ER:29:58:8#2/r1.anchor: Hamza-removal variant of the standard: same root b-w-ʾ but without hamza

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r4.claim: The majority read لنبوئنهم from المباءة, making an abode; cited constructions show بوأ taking two objects or a lām complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r4.anchor: وقرأ: لنبوئنهم، من المباءة. وقرأ علي، وعبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r5.speaker: علي وعبد الله والربيع بن خثيم وابن وثاب وطلحة وزيد بن علي وحمزة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r5.claim: These readers derive the form from الثواء, meaning to remain; this intransitive verb becomes transitive with causative hamza or doubling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r5.anchor: وقرأ: لنبوئنهم، من المباءة. وقرأ علي، وعبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r6.claim: The abode reading means God makes believers a dwelling and refuge; غرف are upper chambers, construed as a direct object or as a locative with a dropped preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r6.anchor: والمعنى: ليجعلن لهم مكان مباءة، أي مرجعا يأوون إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads غرف with a rounded rāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r7.anchor: وروي عن ابن عامر: غرفا، بضم الراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r8.speaker: ابن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r8.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads فنعم with an added fāʾ; the majority omit it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p364/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب: فنعم، بالفاء والجمهور: بغير فاء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.claim: Lanubawwi'annahum means settling them permanently; the oath and its answer together form the predicate of alladhina, against Tha'lab's ban on an oath and its answer serving as a predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r1.anchor: أي لننزلنهم على وجه الإقامة وجملة القسم وجوابه خبر المبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the chambers are elevated halls and splendid palaces of pearl, beryl, and ruby; ghurafan is the second object of the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r2.anchor: أي علالي وقصورا جليلة لا قصور فيها وهي على ما روى عن إبن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.claim: Ali, Abdullah, al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, Ibn Waththab, Talha, Zayd ibn Ali, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read lanuthwiyannahum from thawā, meaning to reside; ghurafan may be its object, governed by an omitted preposition, or an extended locative accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعبدالله والربيع بن خيثم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.claim: Ibn Amir reads ghurufan with a damma on rāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r4.anchor: وروى عن إبن عامر أنه قرأ ( غرفا ) بضم الراء

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.claim: The river clause describes the chambers, while abiding in them refers either to the chambers or to Paradise.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r5.anchor: صفة لغرفا ( خالدين فيها ( أي في الغرف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.claim: How excellent is the workers' wage praises their good works, with its specific referent omitted; alternatively, the distinguishing noun is omitted and the phrase means an excellent wage is the wage of workers.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r6.anchor: أي الأعمال الصالحة والمخصوص بالمدح محذوف ثقة بدلالة ما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.speaker: ابن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.claim: Ibn Waththab adds fa in fa-niʿma to signal sequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p10#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ إبن وثاب ( فنعم ) بفاء الترتيب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r4.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r4.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read nubawwiʾannahum with thāʾ unhamzated, from thawa, meaning to stay; the verb means to settle them in a dwelling.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة، والكسائي: بالثاء ساكنة من غير همز، يقال: ثوى الرجل إذا أقام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r5.claim: The other readers use the bāʾ form with fatḥa, doubled wāw, and hamza, meaning We shall lodge them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p252/r5.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالباء وفتحها وتشديد الواو وهمزة بعدها، أي: لننزلنهم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.claim: God will lodge believers who do good in elevated rooms in Paradise, where rivers flow and they remain; a reading adds fa, and the praised object after niʿma is omitted.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r2.anchor: أي لنقيمنهم من الثواء فيكون انتصاب غرفا لإجرائه مجرى لننزلنهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read lanuthwiyannahum from residence; غرفا is accusative by analogy with lanunzilannahum, omitted preposition, or treating a limited place like an indefinite one.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:57-60/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي «لنثوينهم» أي لنقيمنهم من الثواء فيكون انتصاب غرفا لإجرائه مجرى لننزلنهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r6.claim: Though the passage could describe punishment for defective faith, it omits that warning because the immediate aim is to encourage belief in any measure, and promises believers who do good deeds elevated rooms in Paradise.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r6.anchor: وكان القصد هنا الترغيب في الإيمان كيفما كان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r7.claim: God's promise to lodge the believers in gardens is emphatic; Hamza and al-Kisa'i read the verb with thāʾ from thawa, meaning to dwell.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r7.anchor: وقريب من هذا المعنى قراءةة حمزة والكسائي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r8.claim: The gardens' tall rooms overlook rivers, orchards, fields, and flowers; their residents remain forever without any discomfort prompting them to leave.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r8.anchor: أنهار , إلا كان به بساتين كبار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r9.claim: The reward is excellent, and its workers are defined by enduring patience through difficult duties such as migration until patience becomes their settled character.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p571/r9.anchor: أوجدوا هذه الحقيقة حتى استقرت عندهم فكانت سجية لهم

NASHR:v2p343/r19.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r19.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف
NASHR:v2p343/r19.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf read with thā and substitute ya for the hamza, deriving the form from الثواء, meaning residence.
NASHR:v2p343/r19.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بالثاء المثلثة ساكنة بعد النون وإبدال الهمزة ياء من الثواء، وهو الإقامة

NASHR:v2p343/r20.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p343/r20.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p343/r20.claim: The remaining readers read with bā and hamza, deriving the word from التبوء, a dwelling or lodging; Abu Jafar's hamza substitution was treated earlier.
NASHR:v2p343/r20.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالباء الموحدة والهمز من (التبوء) وهو المنزل
